questions.title: True statement about rheumatic fever
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about rheumatic fever?

options.A: It most commonly affects adults above the age of 25 years.
options.C: It may be complicated by acute infective endocarditis.
options.D: It may be complicated by subacute infective endocarditis.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Rheumatic fever is a disease of CHILDREN and young people (typically 5-15 years), following streptococcal pharyngitis; it is not primarily a disease of adults over 25.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Rheumatic fever follows a group A beta-haemolytic STREPTOCOCCAL (Streptococcus pyogenes) pharyngitis, not a staphylococcal infection; the injury is immune-mediated (molecular mimicry), not a direct bacterial invasion.
explanations.C: Incorrect. ACUTE infective endocarditis is caused by virulent organisms (e.g. Staphylococcus aureus) attacking previously NORMAL valves; a rheumatic-damaged valve is the substrate for the subacute, not the acute, form.
explanations.D: Correct. Rheumatic fever scars and deforms the heart valves (chronic rheumatic valve disease), and these previously DAMAGED valves are the classic substrate seeded by low-virulence organisms (Streptococcus viridans) to produce SUBACUTE infective endocarditis. So subacute infective endocarditis is a recognised late complication of rheumatic valve disease. This contrasts with acute infective endocarditis, which strikes previously normal valves, and it is why a patient with old rheumatic valve disease is at risk of an insidious subacute endocarditis.

questions.learning_objective: Recognise subacute infective endocarditis (on the damaged valve) as a complication of rheumatic fever, and reject the false epidemiology/etiology distractors.
questions.author_notes: The 2008-2015 additional set is UNMARKED in the source (0 red on this item); key D is by medical adjudication of the single true statement. Main concept reuses the subacute-IE-affects-damaged-valves concept (CON-CVS-8FC8A80785631B) since D is exactly that fact applied to rheumatic valve disease; RF-immune-mediated concept (CON-CVS-41547BEDC714F8) linked as contextual for the false etiology/epidemiology distractors. Not a duplicate: the composite 'which is true about RF' stem tests four distinct RF propositions and is a distinct printed item.

questions.title: Site of focal embolic glomerulonephritis (flea-bitten kidney)
questions.question: Focal embolic glomerulonephritis (flea-bitten kidney) occurs in:

explanations.A: Correct. Focal embolic glomerulonephritis (Loehlein's focal embolic nephritis), giving the petechial 'flea-bitten' kidney, is the classic renal lesion of SUBACUTE infective endocarditis. Small septic/immune-complex emboli from the friable valve vegetations of Streptococcus viridans lodge in glomerular capillaries, producing scattered FOCAL segmental necrosis and haemorrhage over the cortical surface. The insidious low-grade bacteraemia of the subacute form, seeding previously damaged valves, is what generates the showers of small emboli that pepper the kidney.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Acute infective endocarditis (virulent organisms on normal valves) tends to throw larger SEPTIC emboli that cause renal infarcts and abscesses rather than the small-vessel focal embolic glomerulonephritis pattern typical of the subacute form.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Generic immune-complex glomerulonephritis is characteristically DIFFUSE (all glomeruli, global involvement), not the focal embolic 'flea-bitten' pattern; the flea-bitten kidney here is specifically the embolic lesion of subacute endocarditis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Systemic lupus erythematosus produces immune-complex lupus nephritis (commonly diffuse proliferative), and its cardiac lesion is sterile Libman-Sacks endocarditis; it is not the cause of focal embolic (flea-bitten) glomerulonephritis.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute focal embolic (flea-bitten) glomerulonephritis to subacute infective endocarditis, distinguishing it from diffuse immune-complex GN and lupus nephritis.
questions.author_notes: Red key A confirmed (pagetext keys p.25). New concept minted for the renal focal-embolic-GN manifestation (distinct from the peripheral embolic stigmata concept CON-CVS-CAF69B8F78112F tested by Q73). Note: the term 'flea-bitten kidney' is also used for the petechial kidney of MALIGNANT hypertension, but the stem qualifies it as focal embolic glomerulonephritis, which is the subacute-IE lesion; contextual link to the subacute-IE-damaged-valves concept.
